cards.title: How Parents and Adult Kids Can Live Together
cards.body: With record numbers of adult children living at home, experts recommend setting clear ground rules from the start and respecting each other's privacy. Avoid reverting to old parent-child dynamics to make the arrangement work for everyone.

cards.title: Human Connection Matters More Than Tech for Kids
cards.body: A pediatrician explains that loss of human connection—not AI or screens—poses the biggest threat to children's wellbeing. The solution often lies in spending more time talking openly with each other.

cards.title: Why You Should Eat Halloween Candy With Your Kids
cards.body: Worried about Halloween candy overload? Ditch restrictive food rules and help your kids build a healthy, guilt-free relationship with food. Breaking free from diet culture benefits their long-term eating habits.

cards.title: Repeating Words: A Developmental Phase Explained
cards.body: Echolalia—repeating other people's words—is a normal part of toddler language development. It can also reveal important things about autism, communication, and how the brain learns.

cards.title: Emotion Regulation: The Skill That Matters Most
cards.body: Teaching emotion regulation early can strengthen children's ability to handle challenges throughout life. Families, schools, and communities can all play a role in building this foundational skill.

cards.title: Understanding Masking and Autism in Children
cards.body: Autistic children often mask or hide their neurodivergent traits to fit in socially. Many report complicated feelings about this coping strategy and its impact on their wellbeing.

cards.title: Frustrated With Parenting Advice? Try Something New
cards.body: With countless parenting advice sources available, children don't seem to be doing better overall. Stepping back to try a different approach may help families find what truly works.
